test_description: Verify that downloadExampleFromGitHub accepts a configurable repository URL and uses it instead of the hardcoded myanlabs/converge default, encoding the Framework vs Project mental model that the framework must remain generic
test_assertions: When repoUrl is provided, the function uses it instead of hardcoded myanlabs/converge
CLI command exposes a --repo flag or CONVERGE_EXAMPLES_REPO env var
Hardcoded org/repo strings no longer appear in executable code paths
change_description: Parameterize the repository URL in downloadExampleFromGitHub() by accepting a configurable repoUrl parameter (sourced from CLI flag or CONVERGE_EXAMPLES_REPO env var), removing the hardcoded myanlabs/converge org/repo strings that embed project-specific identity into framework code
why_this_correction: This finding has the highest leverage under the rubric: Correctness (#1) — hardcoding org/repo URLs means the framework produces broken results for any non-myanlabs user. Prevention (#2) — parameterizing project-specific URLs prevents an entire class of 'hardcoded project references' bugs. The alternative findings (stitch-names-in-jsdoc-examples and stitch-in-test-fixtures) are Leakage/Clarity (#4) issues affecting documentation and test fixtures only, not production code paths. A high-severity Abstraction violation that breaks the framework for external users must take priority over medium/low documentation cleanup.
